title: patient-sim
pitch: A voice bot that phones a healthcare AI agent, plays a realistic patient, and files the bugs it finds.
description: Starts a websocket server, has Twilio dial the agent under test, and relays the call audio to the OpenAI Realtime API, which listens and speaks as the patient. Audio stays G.711 mu-law at 8kHz end to end, so nothing is transcoded anywhere, and personas live in YAML rather than in Python. Eleven recorded calls produced eight documented issues, alongside the probes that found nothing, which are recorded too.

title: PathReview
pitch: A retrieval-augmented agent that reads a developer's GitHub, resume and repos and returns evidence-based portfolio feedback.
description: A multi-tool agent orchestrates GitHub analysis, skill extraction, README scoring and market comparison, with retrieval grounding every claim in the user's actual work rather than in generic advice. Guardrails cover bias detection, content filtering, PII scrubbing and prompt-injection defense. Ships as a Dockerized service with database migrations and a dashboard that tracks improvement over time.

title: Provenance Guard
pitch: A backend service that judges whether text was written by a human or generated by AI, and lets creators appeal the verdict.
description: Combines an LLM judgment with pure-Python stylometry, then expresses the result as a calibrated confidence score paired with a plain-language transparency label rather than a bare yes or no. Every decision is logged, and creators can formally appeal a classification they believe is wrong.

title: TakeMeter
pitch: A fine-tuned classifier that sorts football discourse into three quality tiers, benchmarked against a zero-shot LLM baseline.
description: Comments were collected from four different World Cup 2026 match threads so the dataset would not be tied to a single game or storyline, then labelled under a three-way mutually exclusive taxonomy. The fine-tuned classifier is measured head to head against a zero-shot LLM baseline, which makes the cost of fine-tuning an evidenced decision rather than an assumption.

title: FitFindr
pitch: A multi-tool agent that finds secondhand clothing from a plain-language request and works out how to wear it.
description: You describe what you want in ordinary language; the agent searches listings, assembles an outfit against your existing wardrobe, and writes a shareable caption. Tool failures are handled as an expected path rather than as an exception, so a dead tool degrades the answer instead of ending the conversation.

title: CineLog
pitch: A community film-tracking app used as the subject of a structured code review.
description: Users log films they have watched, rate them, and build collections. The project's real output is the review itself: reading an unfamiliar codebase, identifying defects and design problems, and writing the findings up so that another engineer can act on them.

title: Marvel Dashboard
pitch: A dashboard over the Marvel API with summary statistics and a searchable, multi-filter list view.
description: Fetches live API data with React hooks and async/await, then presents summary statistics above a list that can be searched and narrowed by several filters at once. Filters compose rather than replace one another, so a query can be tightened step by step.

title: Campus Bites
pitch: A card-based guide to ten campus food hubs at Minnesota State University Mankato, with locations and links.
description: Ten venues are presented in a responsive card layout, each linking out to its related resource. Built as a self-contained front end with no framework, which keeps the whole thing to a single fast page load.

title: FlashCards
pitch: A guess-then-flip flashcard app with sequential navigation, shuffling, and answer feedback.
description: The user types a guess before the card flips and gets immediate visual feedback on whether it was right. Back and next buttons move through a fixed sequence while a shuffle control randomises the order, so a deck can be drilled in order or at random.

title: Veni Vici
pitch: A random-discovery browser where any attribute you dislike can be banned, and never appears again.
description: Each click issues a fresh API request and renders one result with its image and attributes. Clicking any displayed attribute adds it to a ban list, and banned attributes are excluded from every later request, so the feed narrows as you use it.
